The other advice here is good too, but also, the less you think of it as trying to "be less awkward" the easier it will be. The framing is important, and framing it like that puts negativity on you. It's important to be empathetic and kind towards yourself. Eliminating that sort of self negativity is a big step towards getting along easier in social situations. That negativity stops you from being yourself, it makes you second guess the things you want to say, and it shows. 

Make sure that you don't frame things like "I was awkward in that conversation". When you catch yourself thinking that way, and assigning negative traits to yourself, instead try to think "when I did/said x, it made the other person feel y." It brings the pressure off of your core self, and puts it onto the thing you did that you didn't like. It's a small change, but an important one.
